40586-billie-bradley-and-her-classmates-.creator: Unknown
40586-billie-bradley-and-her-classmates-.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. ou mean--'in spots'?" asked the third of the trio, Laura Jordon. Laura was as fair as Violet was dark, and now her blue eyes darted an anxious glance at her chum. "Do you think we shall find any thin ice?"

41149-the-soul-of-golf.title: The Soul Of Golf
41149-the-soul-of-golf.creator: Unknown
41149-the-soul-of-golf.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. Nearly every one who writes about a game essays to prove that it is similar to "the great game, the game of life." Golf has not escaped; and numberless scribes in endeavouring to account for the fascination of golf have used the old threadbare tale. As a matter of fact, golf is about as unlike the game of life as any game could well be.

arxiv-1609-01722.title: Applying Relativistic Reconnection to Blazar Jets
arxiv-1609-01722.creator: Krzysztof Nalewajko
arxiv-1609-01722.description: Abstract Rapid and luminous flares of non-thermal radiation observed in blazars require an efficient mechanism of energy dissipation and particle acceleration in relativistic active galactic nuclei (AGN) jets. Particle acceleration in relativistic magnetic reconnection is being actively studied by kinetic numerical simulations.

arxiv-2102-10512.title: The effect of DNA bases permutation on surface enhanced Raman scattering spectrum
arxiv-2102-10512.creator: Shimon Rubin ∗, Phuong H.L. Nguyen ∗, Yeshaiahu Fainman
arxiv-2102-10512.description: Abstract Surface enhanced Raman scattering (SERS) process results in a tremendous increase of Raman scattering cross section of molecules adsorbed to plasmonic metals and influenced by numerous physico-chemical factors such as geometry and optical properties of the metal surface, orientation of chemisorbed molecules and chemical environment.

arxiv-2106-06205.title: Time Warps, from Algebra to Algorithms
arxiv-2106-06205.creator: Sam van Gool, Adrien Guatto, George Metcalfe, Simon Santschi
arxiv-2106-06205.description: Abstract Graded modalities have been proposed in recent work on programming languages as a general framework for refining type systems with intensional properties. In particular, continuous endomaps of the discrete time scale, or time warps , can be used to quantify the growth of information in the course of program execution.

arxiv-2109-00903.title: Effect of the output activation function on the probabilities and errors in medical image segmentation
arxiv-2109-00903.creator: Lars Nieradzik, Gerik Scheuermann, Dorothee Saur, Christina Gillmann
arxiv-2109-00903.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Lars Nieradzik, Gerik Scheuermann, Dorothee Saur, Christina Gillmann. The sigmoid activation is the standard output activation function in binary classification and segmentation with neural networks. Still, there exist a variety of other potential output activation functions, which may lead to improved results in medical image segmentation. In this work, we consider how the asymptotic behavior of different output activation and loss functions affects the prediction probabilities and the corresponding segmentation errors.

arxiv-2203-07095.title: Analysing the accuracy of asymptotic approximations in incomplete contact problems
arxiv-2203-07095.creator: M. R. Moore, D. A. Hills
arxiv-2203-07095.description: Abstract The error incurred in the representation of the contact pressure at the edges of incomplete contacts by first order asymptotes is treated, and the maximum value of the relative error found for a range of geometries, both symmetric and non-symmetric.

arxiv-2206-11413.title: Reflections in an Octagonal Mirror Maze
arxiv-2206-11413.creator: David Eppstein
arxiv-2206-11413.description: Abstract Suppose we are given an environment consisting of axis-parallel and diagonal line segments with integer endpoints, each of which may be reflective or non-reflective, with integer endpoints, and an initial position for a light ray passing through points of the integer grid.

arxiv-2305-14265.title: Adapting to Misspecification Thanks: We thank Isaiah Andrews, Manuel Arellano, Dmitry Arkhangelsky, Stéphane Bonhomme, Tom Boot, Xu Cheng, Bryan Graham, Michal Kolesár, Roger Koenker, Lihua Lei, Jesse Shapiro, and Aleksey Tetenov for helpful discussions on this project. The paper also benefited from
arxiv-2305-14265.creator: Timothy B. Armstrong, Patrick Kline, Liyang Sun
arxiv-2305-14265.description: Abstract Empirical research typically involves a robustness-efficiency tradeoff. A researcher seeking to estimate a scalar parameter can invoke strong assumptions to motivate a restricted estimator that is precise but may be heavily biased, or they can relax some of these assumptions to motivate a more robust, but variable, unrestricted estimator.

arxiv-2306-04735.title: Using Soft-Prompt Tuning to Evaluate Bias in Large Language Models
arxiv-2306-04735.creator: Jacob-Junqi Tian, David Emerson, Sevil Zanjani Miyandoab, Deval Pandya, Laleh Seyed-Kalantari, Faiza Khan Khattak
arxiv-2306-04735.description: Abstract Prompting large language models (LLMs) has gained substantial popularity as pre-trained LLMs are capable of performing downstream tasks without requiring large quantities of labelled data ( Liu et al. 2023 ) . It is, therefore, natural that prompting is also used to evaluate biases exhibited by these models. However, achieving good task-specific performance often requires manual prompt optimization.

Tam et al. 2022 ; Rossi et al. 2022 ; Krieger et al. 2022 . In their comment Pelliciari et al. 2023 on these reports, Pelliciari et al.

arxiv-2403-07400.title: Boundedness of energy for N-body Schrödinger equations with time dependent small potentials
arxiv-2403-07400.creator: Kenji Yajima
arxiv-2403-07400.description: Abstract . We prove that Sobolev norms of solutions to time dependent Schrödinger equations for d d -dimensional N N -partcles interacting via time dependent two body potentials are bounded in time if certain Lebesgue norms of the potentials are small uniformly in time.

arxiv-2406-11820.title: Composing Object Relations and Attributes for Image-Text Matching
arxiv-2406-11820.creator: Khoi Pham, Chuong Huynh, Ser-Nam Lim, Abhinav Shrivastava
arxiv-2406-11820.description: Abstract We study the visual semantic embedding problem for image-text matching. Most existing work utilizes a tailored cross-attention mechanism to perform local alignment across the two image and text modalities. This is computationally expensive, even though it is more powerful than the unimodal dual-encoder approach.

arxiv-2410-03149.title: JASMINE image simulator forhigh-precision astrometry and photometry
arxiv-2410-03149.creator: Takafumi Kamizuka, Hajime Kawahara, Ryou Ohsawa, Hirokazu Kataza, Daisuke Kawata, Yoshiyuki Yamada, Teruyuki Hirano, Kohei Miyakawa, Masataka Aizawa, Masashi Omiya, Taihei Yano, Ryouhei Kano, Takehiko Wada, Wolfgang Löffler, Michael Biermann, Pau Ramos, Naoki Isobe, Fumihiko Usui, Kohei Hattori, Sat
arxiv-2410-03149.description: Abstract JASMINE is a Japanese planned space mission that aims to reveal the formation history of our Galaxy and discover habitable exoEarths. For these objectives, the JASMINE satellite performs high-precision astrometric observations of the Galactic bulge and high-precision transit monitoring of M-dwarfs in the near-infrared (1.0–-1.6 μ \mu m in wavelength).

arxiv-2410-13683.title: Stochastic inflation beyond slow roll: noise modelling and importance sampling
arxiv-2410-13683.creator: David Wands
arxiv-2410-13683.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by David Wands. We simulate the distribution of very rare, large excursions in the primordial density field produced in models of inflation in the very early universe which include a strong enhancement of the power spectrum. The stochastic δ ​ 𝒩 \delta{\mathcal{N}} formalism is used to identify the probability distribution for the primordial curvature perturbation with the first-passage-time distribution, P ⁡ ( δ ​ 𝒩 ) P(\delta{\mathcal{N}}) , and we compare our stochastic results with those obtained in the classical δ ​ 𝒩 \delta{\mathcal{N}} approach.

arxiv-2412-05808.title: SizeGS: Size-aware Compression of 3D Gaussian Splatting via Mixed Integer Programming Thanks: ∗ Shuzhao Xie and Jiahang Liu contributed equally to this research. Thanks: † Corresponding author
arxiv-2412-05808.creator: Shuzhao Xie ∗, Jiahang Liu ∗, Weixiang Zhang, Shijia Ge, Sicheng Pan, Chen Tang, Yunpeng Bai, Cong Zhang, Xiaoyi Fan, Zhi Wang †
arxiv-2412-05808.description: Abstract . Recent advances in 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) have greatly improved 3D reconstruction. However, its substantial data size poses a significant challenge for transmission and storage. While many compression techniques have been proposed, they fail to efficiently adapt to fluctuating network bandwidth, leading to resource wastage.

arxiv-2501-10821.title: Solar oblateness & asphericities temporal variations: outstanding some unsolved issues Volume: 354 Journal: Solar and Stellar Magnetic Fields: Origins and Manifestations
arxiv-2501-10821.creator: Jean P. Rozelot 1, Alexander G. Kosovichev 2, Ali Kilcik 3
arxiv-2501-10821.description: Abstract Solar oblateness has been the subject of several studies dating back to the nineteenth century. Despite difficulties, both theoretical and observational, tangible results have been achieved. However, variability of the solar oblateness with time is still poorly known. How the solar shape evolves with the solar cycle has been a challenging problem.

arxiv-2501-12773.title: Low-Complexity Channel Estimation for RIS-Assisted Multi-User Wireless Communications Thanks: This work was supported by InterDigital. Lajos Hanzo would like to acknowledge the financial support of the Engineering and Physical Sciences Research Council (EPSRC) projects under grant EP/Y037243/1, EP/W
arxiv-2501-12773.creator: Qingchao Li 1 , Mohammed El-Hajjar 1 , Ibrahim Hemadeh 2 , Arman Shojaeifard 2 , and Lajos Hanzo 1
arxiv-2501-12773.description: Abstract Reconfigurable intelligent surfaces (RISs) are eminently suitable for improving the reliability of wireless communications by jointly designing the active beamforming at the base station (BS) and the passive beamforming at the RIS. Therefore, the accuracy of channel estimation is crucial for RIS-aided systems.

arxiv-2503-02396.title: Giant moment increase by ultrafast laser light
arxiv-2503-02396.creator: Sangeeta Sharma, Deepika Gill, Jyoti Krishna, Eddie Harris-Lee, John Kay Dewhurst, Sam Shallcross
arxiv-2503-02396.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Sangeeta Sharma, Deepika Gill, Jyoti Krishna, Eddie Harris-Lee, John Kay Dewhurst, Sam Shallcross. It is now well established that a few femtosecond laser pulse will induce an ultrafast loss of moment in a magnetic material. Here we show that the opposite effect can also occur: an ultrafast increase in moment.

europmc-pmc3084247.description: Background Constitutively active androgen receptor variants (AR-V) lacking the ligand binding domain (LBD) may promote the development of castration-resistant prostate cancer (CRPC). The expression of AR-Vs in the clinically most important metastatic site, the bone, has, however

jewish-encyclopedia-1906-london-solomon-.creator: Herman Rosenthal, N. T. London

pmc-10571294.title: A qualitative exploration of young people’s mental health needs in rural and regional Australia: engagement, empowerment and integration
pmc-10571294.creator: Christiane Klinner, Nick Glozier, Margaret Yeung, Katrina Conn, Alyssa Milton
pmc-10571294.description: BackgroundAustralian rural and regional communities are marked by geographic isolation and increasingly frequent and severe natural disasters such as drought, bushfires and floods. These circumstances strain the mental health of their inhabitants and jeopardise the healthy mental and emotional development of their adolescent populations. Professional mental health care in these communities is often inconsistent and un-coordinated.

pmc-10609278.title: Immunoinformatic Execution and Design of an Anti-Epstein–Barr Virus Vaccine with Multiple Epitopes Triggering Innate and Adaptive Immune Responses
pmc-10609278.creator: Naveed Ahmed, Ali A Rabaan, Ameen S S Alwashmi, Hawra Albayat, Mutaib M Mashraqi, Ahmad A Alshehri, Mohammed Garout, Wesam A Abduljabbar, Nik Yusnoraini Yusof, Chan Yean Yean, Hirokazu Kimura
pmc-10609278.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). One of the most important breakthroughs in healthcare is the development of vaccines. The life cycle and its gene expression in the numerous virus-associated disorders must be considered when choosing the target vaccine antigen for Epstein–Barr virus (EBV). The vaccine candidate used in the current study will also be effective against all other herpesvirus strains, based on the conservancy study, which verified that the protein is present in all herpesviruses.

pmc-11364048.title: Data of history: An open-source and multiformat wall image dataset of Panam city, a historical place
pmc-11364048.creator: Md Taimur Ahad, Yousuf Rayhan Emon, Sumaya Mustofa
pmc-11364048.description: Historical data on monuments offers valuable insights into that period's past sculpture, architecture, and preferences. Realising the importance of historical data and the scarcity of data on historical places, this study presents a dataset collected from Panam City. Panam City, established in the late 1300s century, was the capital of the fifteenth-century Bengal ruler Isa Khan.

pmc-11644513.title: Study on the Mechanical and Thermal Properties and Shape Memory Behaviors of Blends of Bio-Based Polybenzoxazine and Polycaprolactone with Different Molecular Weights
pmc-11644513.creator: Sunan Tiptipakorn, Naritsara Chaipakdee, Sarawut Rimdusit, Kasinee Hemvichian, Pattra Lertsarawut
pmc-11644513.description: In this research, blends of bio-based polybenzoxazine (V-fa) and polycaprolactone (PCL) with different molecular weights (Mn) (14,000, 45,000, and 80,000 Da) were prepared with varying PCL content from 10 to 95 wt%. The spectra measured using Fourier Transform Infrared Spectroscopy (FTIR) may indicate the presence of hydrogen bonding between two polymeric components.

pmc-12538116.title: Continuity of care in Klinefelter syndrome: age-adapted modules for standardized clinical data collection (I-KS)
pmc-12538116.creator: Corinna Grasemann, Claus H Gravholt, Lexi Breen, Lise Aksglaede, Angela Lucas-Herald, Malika Alimussina, Claudia Boettcher, Joline Wernsmann, Jens J Bauer, Jillian Bryce, Francesco Carlomagno, Sabine E Hannema, Andrea Isidori, Inas Mazen, Anna Nordenstroem, S Faisal Ahmed
pmc-12538116.description: Klinefelter syndrome (KS) is an underdiagnosed condition, affecting approximately 1 in 600 male births. Despite its relatively high prevalence, more than two-thirds of affected individuals remain undiagnosed, and clinical awareness is limited. KS presents with a highly variable phenotype, requiring lifelong, multidisciplinary care that spans pediatric and adult specialties.

pmc-12982070.title: Decoding the role of macrophage LAP3 in lung cancer – integration of single-cell technologies and machine learning reveals an orchestrating immunometabolic circuit at the tumor-epithelial interface
pmc-12982070.creator: Yunlong Dong, Xibin Fei, Mengmeng Jiang, Hongsheng Guo, Wencheng Zhang, Xu Chang, Xuanguang Li, Hongjie Zhao, Guangshun Wang
pmc-12982070.description: BackgroundAmino acid metabolism plays a crucial role in shaping tumor–immune crosstalk in non–small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). However, the key cellular mediators that translate metabolic states into intercellular signals remain poorly defined.MethodsWe integrated single-cell RNA-seq with spatial transcriptomics to map immunometabolic architecture.

pmc-13023060.title: Cross-sectional and longitudinal functional network alterations associated with subthreshold depressive symptoms in healthy older adults
pmc-13023060.creator: Pascal Grumbach, Julia Christl, Camilla Mendl-Heinisch, Natalia Wege, Christiane Jockwitz, Eva Meisenzahl, Svenja Caspers
pmc-13023060.description: ObjectiveSubthreshold depressive symptoms (SDS) in older adults as a prodromal state of late-life depression (LLD) increase with age and are associated with elevated risk for cardio- and cerebrovascular diseases. LLD has been linked to functional brain network disruptions, including the ventral attention (VAN) and default mode network (DMN).

pmc-13089662.title: Spatial Learning in Naturalistic Search With Simulated Vision Loss
pmc-13089662.creator: Kirsten Veerkamp, Daniel Müller, Christian N. L. Olivers, David L. Mann
pmc-13089662.description: PurposeIn everyday life, we learn to find relevant objects in complex three-dimensional environments. This spatial learning is even more important under conditions of visual impairment. Yet, little is known about how spatial learning and impaired vision interact to shape search behavior in complex naturalistic settings.

pmc-13199611.title: Eosinophilic Depletion with Benralizumab, Mepolizumab, and Depemokimab: A Modeling Study
pmc-13199611.creator: Pradeep B Lukka, Robert C Penland, Ari Brekkan, Rami Ayoun Alsoud, Sherri So, David W Boulton
pmc-13199611.description: PurposeAnti-interleukin (IL)-5/IL-5 receptor therapies are an integral part of the management of patients with severe eosinophilic asthma. We modeled and compared the blood eosinophil (bEOS) depletion response following indicated dosing regimens with benralizumab, mepolizumab, and depemokimab.MethodsPharmacokinetic (PK)/pharmacodynamic (PD) models were developed to describe antibody concentration and bEOS count in adults.

pmc-13230259.title: Questionable Research Practices: A Principled Classification and Ranking Based on Survey Data
pmc-13230259.creator: Daniele Fanelli, Alan Voodla, Siim Andres, Andero Uusberg
pmc-13230259.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Questionable Research Practices (QRPs) are a highly diverse set of behaviours that eludes clear definition and demarcation. This study collects and organises definitions of QRPs given in surveys, and ranks them by frequency of reported engagement. We systematically retrieved surveys that asked researchers about their engagement with QRPs, and organised these survey definitions in two non-arbitrary classifications based, respectively, on the area of research affected by the QRP (e.g.

pmc-13321593.title: Epigenetic g predicts cognitive function in a diverse, nationally representative sample of older adults
pmc-13321593.creator: Jessica D. Faul, Stacey Collins, Trey Smith, Eric T. Klopack, Colter Mitchell, Eileen M. Crimmins, Mateo P. Farina
pmc-13321593.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundAlzheimer’s disease and related dementias (ADRD) are major public health concerns. DNA methylation (DNAm)–based biomarkers such as GrimAge and PhenoAge predict aging and health risk, but were not designed to optimize prediction of cognitive function or decline.

pmc-13582435.title: Causes of interspecific variation in avian migration distance
pmc-13582435.creator: Neil Paprocki, Courtney J. Conway
pmc-13582435.description: Migration is an awe‐inspiring behavior employed by a diverse suite of taxa throughout the animal kingdom. Avian migration is arguably the most well‐known animal behavior and birds vary widely in how far they migrate, but the ecological mechanisms underlying interspecific variation in migration distance remain unclear.

uslaw-cfr-t45-s2516-100.creator: Corporation For National And Community Service
uslaw-cfr-t45-s2516-100.description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 45 (Public Welfare), Part 2516 (School-Based Service-Learning Programs).
